# v1.1.0-dev.56 - A Load stops when it is done

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.55`.

## Loads No Longer Keep Moving Windows Afterwards

Every Load used to schedule a chain of retries that re-ran the restore at
1.5s, 5.5s, 13.5s, 28.5s, 58.5s and 118.5s. The app kept repositioning
windows for nearly two minutes after you pressed the hotkey, which is
long enough that the movement looked like it came from nowhere.

Worse, each retry re-matched against whatever was on screen at that
moment, and the last matching tier pairs on process name alone. If you
opened a new Explorer or Chrome window forty seconds after loading a
profile that had a missing entry for that process, the retry treated your
brand new window as the missing one and dragged it into a slot it was
never part of.

A Load is now a single pass and it's finished when it returns. Nothing
moves after that.

The trade is real and worth knowing about. An app that opens its windows
slowly, like a cold JetBrains start floating its Build and Terminal
panels a minute in, will now be missed rather than caught late. The load
notification already reports how many of the saved windows were restored
and links to the full report, so an incomplete restore shows up instead
of passing quietly. Hit the hotkey again once the app has settled.

This also fixes the reporting blind spot. Load details is written the
moment the pass finishes, so it used to describe only the first instant
of a Load and none of the retries. There's one pass now, and the report
covers it.

## Reporting A Bug Actually Reaches Somewhere

Settings, then Diagnostics, then "Report a bug" opened an issue against
the private source repo, so every user got a 404. It now opens a
pre-filled issue form on the public releases repo, which works. There's a
"Request a feature" button next to it.

Both open a form in the app first, showing exactly what will be sent
before anything leaves your machine, with the diagnostics dump optional
and your Windows username stripped out of the paths. At time of writing
the form hands off to GitHub in the browser, which still asks for an
account. The account-free path is built but not switched on yet.

## Also

- The support chip in the status bar no longer glitches. That effect was
  meant for the website, not for something sitting in your peripheral
  vision while you work.
- The "Re-apply windows that open late after a Load" setting is gone,
  since there's nothing left for it to turn off.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
